valuation_philosophy: Chorus is a regulated, high-leverage, income-oriented fibre network utility, not a growth compounder. The correct framing is dividend-plus-modest-growth (FY2026 dividend 60cps, FY2027 guided minimum 62cps ~7.4% yield at $8.43), underpinned by the Commerce Commission's PQ2 (2025-2028) building-blocks/RAB revenue-and-capex framework and a post-UFB-build capex taper that is inflecting reported FCF from structurally negative (-$258m FY2018) to positive and rising ($368m FY2026 free cash flow for capital allocation per management's own measure). This DCF is built on UNLEVERED (enterprise) owner FCF -- EBIT*(1-cash tax)+D&A-capex, with NO interest deduction -- discounted at WACC, with net debt subtracted once from enterprise value to reach equity value. This is standard enterprise-DCF practice and is essential here because Chorus's REPORTED FCF (OCF-capex, used in the Metrics.csv) is LEVERED (net of ~$175-220m/yr cash interest paid), and discounting levered FCF at WACC while also subtracting net debt would double-count Chorus's leverage. Given a market cap of only ~$3.75bn against ~$3.13bn of FY2026 net debt (net debt is ~83% of market cap and ~4.31x FY26 EBITDA on a net-debt/EBITDA-per-covenant basis of ~4.75x using the company's own gross measure), the equity value is extremely sensitive to WACC -- see the sensitivity matrix, which shows intrinsic value ranging from ~$10.82 at 5% WACC down to ~$5.9-6.2 at 9% WACC on an unchanged FCF path. This is a mechanical consequence of leverage (a fixed-dollar net debt deduction against a discount-rate-sensitive enterprise value), not a modelling artefact.
model: Unlevered owner-FCF enterprise DCF (net debt subtracted once; EV/EBITDA terminal cap binding over Gordon growth) -- regulated RAB/building-blocks infrastructure route per dcf-methods SKILL.md non-US/cyclical adaptations row

growth_rate_rejections.equity_cagr_rejected: Shareholders' equity has COLLAPSED from NZ$1,022m (FY2018) to NZ$430m (H1-2026, 31-Dec-2025), a 3yr CAGR of approximately -18%/yr and 5yr CAGR of approximately -9%/yr. This is NOT economic decline -- it is the mechanical result of Chorus paying dividends (70-90% of net operating FCF policy) that exceed near-zero-to-modest reported net income every year until FY2026 ($37m), steadily eroding the equity base through retained-earnings deficits while the underlying regulated asset base and cash generation are actually IMPROVING. Using equity CAGR as a growth driver would imply a business in terminal decline, which contradicts every operating metric (fibre uptake now 75.9%, EBITDA up 3% YoY to $726m FY26, capex tapering, FY26 net profit $37m up >9x YoY). Equity CAGR is discarded entirely; revenue/EBITDA growth is used instead.
growth_rate_rejections.pe_and_net_income_rejected: Reported net income was near zero or negative FY2023-FY2025 (FY2023 +$25m, FY2024 -$9m, FY2025 +$4m) before stepping up to $37m in FY2026, because ~NZ$400-475m/yr of depreciation & amortisation (post-UFB-build asset base, plus accelerated depreciation on the copper network being retired by end-CY2028) and ~NZ$175-220m/yr of cash interest on ~NZ$3.1-3.3bn of debt consume most of EBIT. A trailing P/E multiple on Chorus remains distorted by this history and is not used anywhere in this valuation or in the sanity check (P/B and EV/EBITDA are used instead).

Precise FY2026 balance-sheet total-debt/cash split not yet available -- the FY2026 annual report has not been extracted (only the H1 FY2026, 31-Dec-2025, interim report is in Extracted/); net_debt of $3,129m (FY25 $3,057m + disclosed $72m increase) is used as the more current anchor over the H1-2026 net debt of $3,175m (total debt $3,336m - cash $161m), which is six months stale and reflects a different seasonal working-capital point. shares_outstanding/total_debt/cash fields above are retained at the H1-2026 (last full balance sheet on file) level for component detail; net_debt itself uses the FY26 year-end figure. Re-anchor to the FY2026 annual report's exact balance sheet once extracted.

This is a transaction on the CROWN's side of the NIFFCo structure, not a repayment or restructuring of CHORUS's own debt or CIP securities -- Chorus has explicitly stated it does not anticipate material changes to the terms and conditions of its own securities as a result. ASSUMPTION MADE (unchanged from the prior build): net debt above is left UNADJUSTED for this event.

inputs.notes: Model: unlevered owner-FCF enterprise DCF via dcf-methods SKILL.md routing -- Chorus is a regulated network infrastructure operator (Commerce Commission building-blocks/RAB PQ2 regime), not a bank/REIT/LIC/developer/distressed name, so it takes the owner-FCF DCF route with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (leases already expensed under NZ IFRS with no material lease liability separate from total debt; no NCI; no material non-operating assets requiring a bridge item beyond net debt). Net debt is subtracted ONCE from enterprise value; leverage risk lives in the WACC/entry-price sensitivity and dividend-yield framing, not stacked elsewhere. This is an UPDATE of the 2026-08-10-vintage DCF; see reconciliation block.

historical_growth.eps_note: EPS/net income CAGR not computed -- meaningless given near-zero/negative net income FY2023-25 and a single strong FY2026 print ($37m); see growth_rate_rejections.pe_and_net_income_rejected.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: Unchanged from prior build: reported and owner FCF CAGRs are not computable over 3yr/5yr windows because the FY2018/FY2020 base years were structurally negative (UFB build capex peak). FY2022->FY2026 grew off a tiny base as capex tapered -- illustrative of the inflection, not a repeatable growth rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-9% to -18%/yr) diverges enormously (>30%) from Revenue/EBITDA CAGR (+1-2%/yr). Per growth_rate_rejections.equity_cagr_rejected, this divergence is a DISTRIBUTION-POLICY artefact, not an operating signal; equity CAGR is discarded as the growth driver in favour of revenue/EBITDA, the metrics the Commerce Commission's RAB/PQ regime actually caps and grows.
historical_growth.notes: Growth here is REGULATED (Commerce Commission building-blocks/RAB regime under PQ2, 2025-2028), not market-driven. Year-1 (FY2027) is now anchored to management's own guidance (EBITDA $730-760m, up from FY26 actual $726m) rather than purely a historical CAGR extrapolation -- this is the one driver year materially re-judged on new evidence in this update. Years 2-10 retain the prior build's taper logic (RAB+CPI-linked revenue growth tapering to terminal 2.3%, EBITDA margin rising toward 72.3% as copper retirement removes legacy opex, D&A tapering off the accelerated copper-depreciation peak, cash tax ramping from CIP-shelter-suppressed low starting rates toward the 28% statutory rate) -- unchanged because no new evidence in this update moved them: FY26 actuals and FY27 guidance both landed within the range the prior build had already projected for these years (see reconciliation).

wacc_rationale.approach: Bottom-up CAPM build, cross-checked against the Commerce Commission's own PQ2 allowed WACC determination.
wacc_rationale.asset_beta_rationale: Regulated network utility with contracted/RAB-set cash flows typically carries a low unlevered/asset beta (0.35-0.45); 0.40 used -- unchanged. Note: the Commerce Commission's 25-Aug-2026 Tranche 1 decision on the 2027 Fibre IM Review signalled a preliminary view (reported mid-Sep-2026) toward REDUCING the assessed systematic risk of fibre businesses for the PQ3 (from 2029) determination, which if it flows through to the Commission's own asset-beta assumption would argue for the low end of the 0.35-0.45 range, not a change today. Final cost-of-capital parameters are due Q4 2026, after this valuation date -- deliberately NOT pre-empted here; see risk_addon_rationale.
wacc_rationale.cost_of_debt_basis: H1 FY2026 weighted average interest rate per company disclosure -- unchanged; Chorus issued EUR400m 7-year notes at 3.529% and repurchased EUR243m of 2026-maturity notes at 81.5% of face in Feb-2026, consistent with this cost-of-debt level.
wacc_rationale.capital_weights_basis: Market-value weights: FY26 net debt $3,129m / equity market cap ~$3,751m at current price $8.43 x 445m shares.
wacc_rationale.regulatory_cross_check: The Commerce Commission has SET Chorus's allowed WACC at 7.68% PRE-TAX for the PQ2 period (1-Jan-2025 to 31-Dec-2028). Converted to a rough post-tax equivalent at the 28% statutory rate, that is approximately 5.53% post-tax -- broadly consistent with (slightly below) the ~5.9% bottom-up build. The regulatory figure uses the regulator's notional benchmark gearing for the RAB, not Chorus's actual capital structure or equity-holder risk, and does not price PQ3 (2029 reset) uncertainty or refinancing risk.
wacc_rationale.risk_addon_rationale: Held UNCHANGED in this update (base WACC still 7.0%), deliberately not moved ahead of the Commerce Commission's Q4-2026 final cost-of-capital determination for PQ3, despite the Aug/Sep-2026 preliminary signal toward lower assessed systematic risk for fibre. That signal, if it firms up, is the upside catalyst already captured qualitatively in the bull scenario's lower WACC (6.3%) and reflected as the single largest swing factor named in the guidance commentary. Moving the base case WACC now on a preliminary, non-final regulatory signal would be pre-empting a determination that has not yet been made; the addon continues to reflect (a) PQ3 reset uncertainty generally, (b) refinancing/interest-rate risk on the EUR/AUD medium-term note stack recurring through 2032, and (c) leverage at the top of Chorus's own 4.75x net-debt/EBITDA policy tolerance (FY26 actual ~4.75x, no headroom), which if anything argues against lowering the addon this cycle even as the regulatory-risk component of it may ultimately fall.
wacc_rationale.bull_bear_rationale: Bull reflects the Commerce Commission's preliminary lower-systematic-risk signal for fibre being confirmed at the Q4-2026 PQ3 determination plus an improving credit profile (S&P positive outlook) compressing WACC toward the bottom-up/regulatory-cross-check range; bear reflects an adverse PQ3 reset (assessed risk NOT reduced, or RAB rollforward pressured), higher-for-longer refinancing rates, and leverage stress given FY26 net debt/EBITDA is already at the ~4.75x policy ceiling with no headroom.

base.assumption_notes: Year-1 (FY2027) RE-JUDGED on new evidence: revenue growth and EBITDA margin now anchored directly to management's FY2027 guidance (EBITDA $730-760m, midpoint $745m against FY2026 actual $726m = +2.6% implied growth; gross capex $375-415m, midpoint $395m). Years 2-10 UNCHANGED from the prior (2026-08-10) build's taper logic: revenue tapering RAB+CPI-linked growth toward long-run 2.3% terminal; EBITDA margin rising toward ~72.3% as copper retirement (full retirement by end-CY2028, i.e. within Year 2 of this horizon) removes legacy network opex; D&A tapering from the still-elevated copper-accelerated-depreciation run-rate toward a ~29% steady state once copper is fully retired; capex tapering toward a derived sustaining-only level of ~$230-240m/yr, consistent with FY2027 guided sustaining capex of $195-215m plus residual growth capex fading as the fibre uptake target (75.9% actual FY26, approaching 80%) is neared; cash tax ramped from a low starting rate (10%, reflecting CIP-notional-interest and Crown-grant-amortisation permanent differences that have kept cash tax paid near zero historically) toward the 28% statutory rate by Year 10. Terminal cap multiple retained at 8.0x EV/EBITDA, the level the prior build's Step-8c sanity check fixed it at (an unconstrained higher cap breached the 10-year historical EV/EBITDA trading range of 5.5x-9.7x); re-verified against the current sanity check below and still holds (implied 9.4x on FY26 actual EBITDA, within range).

bull.assumption_notes: Fibre uptake exceeds prior targets faster (Hyperfibre 70,000-connection target by 2030 additive), ARPU mix-shift and data-centre-adjacent products (Express Connect, Unified Transport, TimeSync) land at the top end, the Commerce Commission's preliminary lower-systematic-risk signal for fibre is confirmed at the Q4-2026 PQ3 determination and credit profile improves (S&P positive outlook realised), compressing WACC and supporting a richer (9.0x) exit multiple -- still requiring some multiple re-rating above the historical ceiling (bull IV implies ~11.7x on FY26 EBITDA vs the 10yr historical ceiling of 9.7x), i.e. the bull case explicitly requires cash-flow delivery AND a re-rating, not cash-flow delivery alone.

bear.assumption_notes: FWA/Starlink substitution caps uptake below management's targets (Starlink already NZ's largest single rural broadband provider per the Commerce Commission's 2025 monitoring report, 27% share), an adverse PQ3 (2029) reset (assessed systematic risk NOT reduced, RAB rollforward pressured) keeps allowed WACC lower for Chorus's regulated revenue while Chorus's own funding costs stay higher-for-longer, copper withdrawal costs run above the accelerated 2028 timetable's plan, and net debt/EBITDA already sitting at the ~4.75x policy ceiling with no headroom triggers de-rating (7.0x, below the historical median of 8.6x) as the market prices in leverage/regulatory risk.

base.fcf_path_used: base case unlevered owner FCF (decelerating growth path, not a constant rate)
base.interpretation: The 15%-IRR entry price of ~$1.80 sits far below both intrinsic value ($8.30) and the current price ($8.43). This is the mechanically correct output, not a formula error: Chorus's projected growth (2.3-2.6%/yr) is far below the 15% hurdle, AND net debt (~$3,129m, a FIXED dollar amount) is ~83% of the current $3.75bn market cap. When cash flows and terminal value are discounted at 15% instead of the 7% WACC, enterprise value shrinks sharply while the fixed net-debt deduction does not -- crushing the thin equity residual. PRACTICALLY: Chorus is not a stock that can be bought today to manufacture a 15% IRR from fundamentals alone -- it is priced (and should be evaluated) as a ~7.4% dividend-yield regulated-utility income holding (FY2027 guided minimum 62cps / $8.43), where the relevant comparison is the WACC-based intrinsic value and the dividend yield, not a growth-IRR entry price. Unchanged conclusion from the prior build.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows are near-flat across terminal growth because the 8.0x EV/EBITDA cap (not Gordon growth) binds the terminal value at every WACC/g combination shown. The real sensitivity is to WACC: intrinsic value ranges from ~$10.82/share at 5% WACC down to ~$5.9-6.2/share at 9% WACC -- an ~80% swing in equity value for a 4-point WACC range, roughly double the swing a similarly-profiled unlevered company would show, the direct consequence of Chorus's leverage (net debt ~83% of market cap). This is the single most important sensitivity in this model and should be surfaced prominently on the dashboard.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged 25/50/25 from the prior build: base case tracks management's own FY2027 guidance closely; bull requires both faster uptake/margin delivery AND a favourable, not-yet-final PQ3 regulatory determination; bear requires either an adverse PQ3 reset or a leverage-driven de-rating given net debt/EBITDA is already at the policy ceiling with no headroom -- roughly symmetric, credible tail risks either side of the base case, warranting equal 25% weights rather than a skew.

dividend_context.payout_policy: 70-90% of net operating free cash flow (after sustaining capex); policy explicitly targets dividend growth at the rate of inflation.
dividend_context.imputation_note: FY2027 guided dividend is expected to carry PARTIAL imputation for the first time (vs fully unimputed FY2026), a new incremental positive for NZ-resident shareholders' after-tax yield not present in the prior build.
dividend_context.note: For an income-oriented holding, the dividend yield (~7.1-7.4% at current price) plus modest inflation-linked dividend growth (now partially imputed from FY2027) is a more intuitive way to frame the expected return than a pure capital-appreciation IRR -- see entry_price.base.interpretation.

fcf_quality_history.note: SBC and interest-income adjustments are immaterial for Chorus (net-DEBT company, trivial KMP-only SBC) -- reported and owner FCF are essentially identical historically. The material adjustment is the LEVERED vs UNLEVERED FCF distinction used in the DCF projections; see valuation_philosophy.
